item.title: CKB Talk Daily Brief - 2026-09-18
item.description: ## 今日发生了什么 从可引用材料看，2026-09-17 的论坛动态集中在项目评审和状态更新上 [S01, S02, S03, S04, S05]。LiquidLane 提案被委员会拒绝 [S02]；CRT 提案状态为 Pending [S03]；Tranfr 完成第一笔付款并重申最终验收标准 [S04]；Dular 项目获得批准 [S05]。Fiber 自动通道流动性再平衡 RFC 被移到 Infrastructure 后，作者称仍未收到技术反馈 [S01]。 ## 重点话题 LiquidLane：委员会完成审核后决定拒绝 LP-backed Fiber channel liquidity 提案，并表示希望透明说明原因 [S02]。 Spark Program | CRT：委员会将 CKB Revocable Timelock 提案状态设为 Pending，并明确这不是拒绝 [S03]。 Tranfr：委员会已完成第一笔付款，并重申最终验收标准是交付功能完整的前端和 SDK [S04]。 Dular：委员会完成最终评估，认为提交者有足够努力和值得称赞的表现，并批准项目 [S05]。 Fiber 流动性再平衡：ILE_LABS 的 RFC 被移到 Infrastructure，但作者表示尚未收到关于问题是否与当前 Fiber 开发相关的技术反馈 [S01]。 ## 值得继续跟进 LiquidLane 被拒后，委员会提到的具体理由尚未在可引用内容中展开，后续可关注完整说明或提案方是否调整 [S02]。 CRT 目前仍为...

item.title: [RFC & Research] Automated Channel Liquidity Rebalancing on Fiber Network (1 posts)
item.description: Following up on this thread. The post has been moved to Infrastructure, but we have not yet received technical feedback on whether the problem is relevant to current Fiber development. The prototype targets a specific gap: Fiber supports manual circular rebalancing through build_router, but operators still have to inspect topology, calculate fees, evaluate timelock exposure, and manage channel capacity manually. Before we invest further, we need to know: Is automated channel-liquidity rebalancing a current Fiber priority? Are the existing build_router and self-payment APIs considered sufficient? item.title: LiquidLane: LP-Backed Fiber Channel Liquidity (1 posts)
item.description: Hello @FidelCoder, Thank you for taking the time to revise the proposal. The committee has completed its review and, after careful consideration, regrets to inform you that it has decided to reject the LiquidLane proposal. We wish to maintain transparency regarding the reasons behind this decision: The funding security and custody solutions are too rudimentary and fail to address the core risks that concern the committee: The proposal states that LPs pool funds in an on-chain vault, with LiquidLane using these funds to deploy Fiber channels and returning the funds to the “fixed recovery lock” upon expiration. However, the proposal does not adequately explain how the custody mechanism...

item.title: Spark Program | CKB Revocable Timelock (CRT) — Timelock Encryption You Can Cancel (1 posts)
item.description: Hi @psawyerberlin, Thank you for your continued interest in the Spark Program and for submitting the CKB Revocable Timelock (CRT) proposal. After review by the Spark Program committee, your proposal has been assigned a status of Pending. This is not a rejection, but an invitation to revise. The committee recognizes the genuine pain point you’ve identified — the inability to revoke or cancel a timelock encryption once scheduled is a real limitation in drand-based systems, and your use cases (VoteSecure, sealed-bid auctions, dead man’s switches) are well-articulated. The concept of leveraging CKB’s cell consumption and type-id uniqueness as a “kill switch” is creative and aligns well with...

item.description: Hi @SalmanDev, The committee has completed the first payment. The first installment (139,527 CKB, 20%) have been disbursed.
